blocks.prompt: 8 Find the minimum distance from the ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{4} = 1\) to the line \(x + y = 6\).
blocks.explanation:
Humein ek curve (ellipse) aur ek line ke darmiyan sab se chhota faasla chahiye.
Pehle yeh tasdeeq zaroori hai ke line ellipse ko kaat'ti to nahi; agar kaat'ti to sab se kam faasla zero hota.
Phir ellipse ke parametric point \((3\cos\theta, 2\sin\theta)\) ka line se perpendicular faasla \(\theta\) ke function ki shakal mein likhenge.
Aakhir mein is function ka minimum nikalenge; tasdeeq ke liye parallel tangent wala tareeqa bhi dekhenge.
Aakhir mein parallel tangent wale tareeqe se bhi isi jawab tak pahunchenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{4} = 1\) (\(a = 3\), \(b = 2\)); line \(x + y = 6\).
Maloom karna: dono ke darmiyan sab se kam faasla.
Tareeqa: ellipse ke point ka line se perpendicular faasla theta ke function ki tarah, phir us ka minimum.

Line ellipse ko nahi milti
Line ko \(y = -x + 6\) likhein: \(m = -1\), \(c = 6\).
\[a^2m^2 + b^2 = 9(1) + 4 = 13\]
\[c^2 = 36 > 13\]
Kyun: \(c^2 > a^2m^2 + b^2\) ho to line ellipse se bilkul bahar hai (6.4.3 ki shart). Agar line kaat'ti to jawab seedha zero hota.

Ellipse ke point ka faasla
\(P(3\cos\theta, 2\sin\theta)\) lein:
\[D(\theta) = \frac{|3\cos\theta + 2\sin\theta - 6|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}}\]
Kyun: point \((x_1, y_1)\) ka line \(Ax + By + C = 0\) se faasla \(\frac{|Ax_1 + By_1 + C|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}}\) hai; yahan \(A = B = 1\), \(C = -6\).

\(3\cos\theta + 2\sin\theta\) ki sab se bari qeemat
\[f(\theta) = 3\cos\theta + 2\sin\theta\]
\[f'(\theta) = -3\sin\theta + 2\cos\theta = 0\]
\[\tan\theta = \frac{2}{3}\]
\[\sin\theta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}, \quad \cos\theta = \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\]
\[f_{\max} = \frac{9}{\sqrt{13}} + \frac{4}{\sqrt{13}} = \sqrt{13}\]
Kyun: inteha (extreme) qeemat par derivative zero hota hai; wahan \(f'' = -f < 0\), is liye yeh maximum hai. \(\tan\theta = \frac{2}{3}\) se triangle ki sides 2, 3 aur \(\sqrt{13}\).

Sab se kam faasla
Har \(\theta\) ke liye \(3\cos\theta + 2\sin\theta \le \sqrt{13} < 6\), is liye modulus ke andar wali qeemat negative hai aur \(D = \frac{6 - (3\cos\theta + 2\sin\theta)}{\sqrt{2}}\). Yeh tab sab se chhota hai jab bracket sab se bara ho:
\[D_{\min} = \frac{6 - \sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \frac{6\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{26}}{2} \approx 1.69\]
Kyun: 6 mein se sab se bari mumkin qeemat ghatane par sab se chhota faasla bachta hai.
Dhyan dein: f ka minimum lena ghalat hoga; us se sab se zyada faasla milta hai.

Ek nazar mein
Curve se line ka sab se kam faasla nikalne ke do raaste hain: parametric point ka faasla minimise karna, ya line ke parallel tangent dhoondna. Doosra raasta aksar chhota hota hai, magar pehle yeh zaroor dekhiye ke line curve ko kaat to nahi rahi.

Tasdeeq
Sab se qareeb point \(\left(\frac{9}{\sqrt{13}}, \frac{4}{\sqrt{13}}\right)\) hai. Wahan tangent line ke parallel hai: \(x + y = \sqrt{13}\) (shart \(c = \sqrt{a^2m^2 + b^2}\) se). \(x + y = 6\) aur \(x + y = \sqrt{13}\) ka faasla \(\frac{6 - \sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{2}}\) hai, wohi jawab.
Kyun: sab se qareeb point par ellipse ka tangent di gayi line ke parallel hota hai; do tareeqon se ek jawab.
